name: Saint Ephrem
history: A deacon of the Syrian Church whose hymns earned him the name Harp of the Holy Spirit. He wrote in Syriac, the language closest to the Aramaic of Christ, and taught the faith to his people through poetry and song, above all on Christ and on the Virgin Mary. Benedict XV named him a Doctor of the Church in 1920.
life: Ephrem was born at Nisibis, on the border between the Roman and Persian empires, and served its bishops as a deacon and teacher. He wrote hundreds of hymns, many for choirs of women to sing, so that sound teaching would be carried in melody against the heresies of his day. His images are rich and concrete: the pearl, the womb, the robe, the medicine of life. When Nisibis was handed to Persia in 363, Ephrem went with the Christian refugees to Edessa, where he taught in the school and lived simply. He never sought the priesthood. In the famine of 372 he organised relief for the hungry, and he died the following year. His writing shaped the worship of the Syriac Churches and later of the Greek and Latin Churches as well.
prayerTo: Saint Ephrem, you sang the mysteries of Christ and of His Mother, and taught the faith with beauty. Pray for the Christians of Syria and Iraq, for all who write and sing for God, and for me, that my praise may be warm and my faith true. Amen.
penance: Sing or listen attentively to a hymn today and pray it as a prayer. Ephrem ended his life feeding the hungry: give something to a famine appeal.
meditation: Ephrem compared the Word of God to a spring that no one can drink dry. Return to one passage today and drink again.
